title: Per-model SLI spectrum and staged failover orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define a pragmatic, machine-readable per-endpoint and per-model SLI/SLO matrix that supports multi-region staged failover and tiered circuit-breaker actions. This ticket codifies the SLI spectra (availability, p50/p95/p99 latency, and output-quality signals), the error-budget burn policies, and the automated orchestration for progressive degradation and cross-region evacuation. Deliverables: 1) canonical SLI manifest (CSV/JSON schema) 2) failover choreography and circuit-breaker thresholds 3) automation hooks for release gates and canary rollbacks 4) runbook and Grafana dashboards linked to SLI anchors.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI manifest published to docs.redwood.ai/reliability/sli-manifest with machine-parseable schema
For top 10 hosted models, define per-model baseline SLOs and graded degradation bands (gold/silver/bronze)
Circuit-breaker actions implemented as policy entries: soft-shed -> hard-evict -> region-failover with automated rollback gates
Dashboards and alert rules created: error-budget burn-rate, cross-region traffic divergence, model-quality drift (semantic-similarity) and displayed in runtime-1.22 release dashboard
Runbook for escalation and emergency rollback documented with postmortem template and linked playbooks
decision_summary: SLIs will be grouped into three orthogonal axes: availability (success rate), latency (quantiles: p50/p95/p99), and quality (semantic-similarity on a representative promptset).
SLOs target per-route 'gold' tier: 99.7% availability, p95 latency < 200ms for short-chat routes; fallback degradation bands set per model for graceful quality/latency trade-offs.

Circuit-breaker will run in two phases: soft-shed (reduce concurrency/batch size, enable kv cache bypass) and hard-evict (fallback to compatible lower-cost variant or queue). Region failover is last-resort and requires both error-budget breach and regional capacity shortage signals.

Error-budget accounting uses a rolling 30-day window with burn-rate evaluation over 6h, 24h, and 7d horizons to decide automated actions; auto-evacuation requires sustained >3x burn-rate over 24h plus capacity alarm.

open_risks: Measuring quality SLI reliably requires a representative promptset per tenant; collection and privacy constraints may delay rollout.
Automated region-evacuation can cause user-visible session loss for chat flows unless KV cache warm-up strategies exist.
Interplay between batching and circuit-breaker soft-shed may increase tail latency temporarily; need careful simulation across model sizes.
tradeoffs: Aggressive soft-shed reduces cost and preserves some capacity but risks quality regressions for long-context models.
Tighter SLOs improve UX but increase operational burden and potential cost; we recommend tiered SLOs (gold/silver/bronze) to align with customer tiers.
Automated rollback gates reduce human toil but add complexity to the control-plane state machine; we'll keep manual override in early rollout.
